note: Literature shows direct terminological and phenotypic divergence between Birnbaum et al. ('syndrome') and Turkyilmaz et al. ('nonsyndromic ID').

evidence.text: Turkyilmaz et al. identified a homozygous stop-gain variant in SGSM3 in two siblings with short stature and ID, framing SGSM3 as a candidate gene for a nonsyndromic intellectual disability phenotype, while referencing Birnbaum et al.'s earlier report.

source.title: A Strong Candidate Gene for Nonsyndromic Intellectual Disability Phenotype: SGSM3
source.quote: The report of two cases with bi-allelic LOF variants in the SGSM3 gene from different populations with similar clinical manifestations strengthens the potential of this gene as a candidate gene for the nonsyndromic ID phenotype.

evidence.text: Birnbaum et al. describe the condition linked to an Ashkenazi Jewish founder variant in SGSM3 as an intellectual disability syndrome.

source.title: Intellectual disability syndrome associated with a homozygous founder variant in SGSM3 in Ashkenazi Jews
source.quote: In this paper, we highlight SGSM3 as a candidate disease gene for autosomal recessive mild to moderate intellectual disability. We identified a founder variant in Ashkenazi Jews
